original_native_abi.ghidra_convention_note: The live decompilation warns 'Unknown calling convention' and renders the body as (PaletteMain * this, uint32_t categoryID) with a return value it places in a synthetic in_ECX. The disassembly contradicts that rendering: ECX is the receiver (MOV ESI,ECX), the tested byte is the low byte of the first ordinary stack word (ESP+0x8 after PUSH ESI), and the returned EAX is the saved receiver, not a value produced by the body.

body_evidence.raw_bytes_note: read live at 0x005c5ee0 length 32; these 30 bytes are exactly the eleven instructions from 0x005c5ee0 through the RET 0x4 at 0x005c5efb-0x005c5efd, and the following 0xcc is padding

observed_mechanics: 0x005c5ee0-0x005c5ee1 push ESI and copy the ECX receiver into ESI, so the receiver word survives both calls and is available for both the release and the return.
0x005c5ee3 calls 0x005c5e90 with no preceding push and with ECX still holding the receiver, so the call carries the receiver and no ordinary stack word.
the EAX result of 0x005c5e90 is discarded, because 0x005c5ef8 loads EAX from ESI before the return.
0x005c5ee8 tests bit 0 of the byte at ESP+0x8. After the PUSH ESI at 0x005c5ee0 that displacement is the low byte of the first ordinary stack word, so only bit 0 of that word is read.
0x005c5eed jumps to 0x005c5ef8 when bit 0 is clear, so the release is skipped without any other test.
0x005c5eef-0x005c5ef5 push ESI, call 0x00f47380 and add 4 back to ESP, so the release is cdecl and the caller reclaims its single argument word.

0x005c5ef8-0x005c5efb load EAX with the saved receiver, restore ESI and return with RET 0x4, so the callee reclaims exactly one four-byte stack word and the receiver word is the returned value on both paths.
the body contains no memory write of any kind: the receiver word is never dereferenced, so no receiver field is read or published by this function.
the body contains no null test, so a null receiver is forwarded unchanged to 0x005c5e90 and, on the release path, to 0x00f47380.

ordinary_stack_arguments: the receiver word, pushed by PUSH ESI at 0x005c5eef

callee_provenance.0x005c5e90: 78 raw bytes, 0x005c5e90 through the RET at 0x005c5edd: PUSH EBX; PUSH EBP; MOV EBP,ECX ... MOV dword ptr [EBP+0x0],0x013ec458; MOV dword ptr [EBP+0x8],0x013eb938; POP EBP; POP EBX; RET. It stores 0x013f7fd4 and 0x013f7fc4 into the two vtable words of its receiver at entry and a second pair before returning, and it reads the words at receiver+0x04 and receiver+0x0c. The live decompilation renders it as a destructor-shaped body with a list teardown loop and a call to 0x005c2230 and to Palettes::PaletteIterator::Next. Its internal loop and the meaning of its two list words are not modeled here.
callee_provenance.0x00f47380: live decompilation is `void FUN_00f47380(int param_1) { if (param_1 != 0) { FUN_009276c0(param_1); } }`, so the port is a null-guarded release with a void return. The behavior inside 0x009276c0 is not modeled.

incoming_edges.note: 0x005c5e83 is the JMP operand of the thunk at 0x005c5e80, whose bytes are `SUB ECX,0x8` then `JMP 0x005c5ee0`. It is a tail transfer, not a call frame, and it exists in the file image at an address Ghidra has not defined as a function.

call_graph.caller_evidence: live ghidra_get_xrefs_to(0x005c5ee0) returns exactly two references: DATA from 0x013f7fd4 and UNCONDITIONAL_CALL from 0x005c5e83. No direct call from a defined function exists, so every observed entry is through a vtable word.
call_graph.dispatch_chain: 0x013f7fcc holds 0x005c5e80, which is the subobject vtable slot at displacement 0x08 of the table at 0x013f7fc4, and that thunk subtracts 8 from ECX before reaching 0x005c5ee0. A dispatch through the receiver+0x08 subobject pointer therefore arrives with the receiver word pre-adjusted to the primary object.

primary_table.adjacent_word_note: 0x00804900 is an instruction-aligned `SUB ECX,0x8; JMP 0x00804e70` thunk, so 0x00804901 is not an instruction start. The word is kept as an opaque modeled slot and no role is claimed for it.

semantic_findings.claim: Bounded teardown plus one conditional release of the receiver, nothing more.
semantic_findings.statement: The body always forwards the receiver to 0x005c5e90, releases the receiver through the cdecl null-guarded wrapper 0x00f47380 only when bit 0 of its single stack word is set, and returns the receiver word itself in EAX. It writes no memory of its own.

identity_conflict.machine_evidence: The imported SDK name is the only source of the GetCategory label; no evidence in the machine code supports a category lookup. The body performs no lookup, dereferences no receiver word, and returns the receiver word rather than a distinct object, and the entry sits at slot 0 of the vtable word stored at receiver+0x00, which is the position an MSVC virtual destructor occupies.
classification_basis: a single ordinary stack word whose bit 0 selects free-or-not is the MSVC deleting-destructor flag argument
0x005c5e90 stores two different pairs of vtable words into its receiver, which is destructor behaviour
the entry occupies vtable slot 0x00 and the adjacent word 0x013f7fd8 is not a proven code pointer, so the modeled table holds one virtual entry
identity_conflict.classification_status: inference, not a recovered source name; no original source identifier, parameter name, or return type is proven
identity_conflict.treatment: The source symbol embeds the SDK label so the validator can locate the span, and the body models only the machine mechanics. The `categoryID` formal and the `PaletteCategory*` return type of the imported label are explicitly not reproduced; the modeled return type is the receiver word, which the disassembly proves.
identity_conflict.unresolved: Whether the original class really was named PaletteMain, whether the argument really was named categoryID, and what the return type was in the original source.

semantic_findings.no_ledger_conflict: No entry in knowledgegraph/research/conflicts was cited for this VA by the briefing, and none was consulted as evidence.

failure_boundaries.null_receiver: Not guarded. The null word is forwarded to 0x005c5e90, which dereferences it at once; on the release path the null word is also forwarded to 0x00f47380, whose own null check makes that second call a no-op. The model reproduces the forwarding, not the fault.
failure_boundaries.stack_word_bit_0_clear: 0x005c5e90 has run and 0x00f47380 has not; the receiver word is still returned.
failure_boundaries.stack_word_bit_0_set: 0x005c5e90 has run, the receiver has been handed to the release wrapper, and the receiver word is still returned afterwards. Whether the original caller inspects a released pointer is not observable here.
failure_boundaries.unusual_stack_word: Only bit 0 is consulted, so words 0x00000002 and 0xfffffffe take the same path as zero.

runtime_gates: Observe a real virtual dispatch through the word at 0x013f7fd4 and through the subobject slot at 0x013f7fcc, and record which of the two produced the entry call and with which receiver word.
Record the receiver words at +0x00, +0x04 and +0x08 before and after the call and confirm that the entry itself leaves all three unchanged.
Observe 0x005c5e90 live: its loop, the callees it invokes, and the values of the words it reads at receiver+0x04 and receiver+0x0c.
Capture both stack-word polarities at a real call site and confirm that only bit 0 decides the release.
Confirm the returned EAX is the receiver word on the release path, where the receiver has just been handed to the release wrapper.
Determine the class and base-subobject binding of the vtables at 0x013f7fd4 and 0x013f7fc4, and the role of the word at 0x013f7fd8.
Resolve whether the original source identifier, argument name, and return type match the imported SDK label or the destructor-shaped reading of the body.
unresolved_questions: The briefing carried no ABI section (evidence.missing_sections listed ABI), so the recorded ABI is derived from the eleven-instruction disassembly plus read-only live Ghidra queries; a repaired calling convention in Ghidra should confirm it.

The live Ghidra signature is (PaletteMain * this, uint32_t categoryID) returning PaletteCategory*, but the decompilation carries the warning 'Unknown calling convention' and renders the return as a synthetic in_ECX. The disassembly proves the return register is EAX and that EAX holds the receiver, so the recorded return type is the receiver word rather than the imported PaletteCategory*.

The briefing vtables evidence recorded vtable:0x013f7fc4 while the live file image stores 0x005c5ee0 at 0x013f7fd4. Which of the two records is authoritative for the triage ledger, and does 0x013f7fc4 need a correction?

Is the entry a deleting destructor, a hand-written release wrapper, or an accessor that the SDK symbol importer mislabeled? The machine mechanics are identical in all three cases, so the classification is unresolved.
What is the argument really named and typed in the original source, given that only its low byte is read?
What class owns the vtable at 0x013f7fd4, what does the adjacent word 0x013f7fd8 = 0x00804901 represent, and why is it one byte into the 0x00804900 thunk?
Which base subobject does the table at 0x013f7fc4 belong to, and what do its four thunk words do besides the -8 adjustment?
What do the words at receiver+0x04 and receiver+0x0c that 0x005c5e90 reads and subtracts represent, and what type do they hold?
Can the returned EAX be a released pointer in the original program, and does any caller use it after the release?
What is the receiver's full layout and allocation size, and can a null receiver ever reach this entry in the original program?
